newsitem.title: USA: Donna Karan selects new chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Donna Karan selects new chief executive.

text.p: Struggling fashion design company Donna Karan Intl. on Monday named an executive from Polo Ralph Lauren Corp. to take over as the company's chief executive officer.

The new chief executive, John Idol, a group president and divisional chief operating officer responsible for the Ralph Lauren Clothing Company, will take up his new position on Aug. 11, Donna Karan said.

He replaces company founder Donna Karan, who will give up the chief executive position but remain chairman and chief designer. The move was not unexpected, as Karan had indicated previously that she would leave the executive position to focus on design and marketing.
In his new position, Idol will be responsible for "strategic leadership," Karan said.

"A global company of this size and complexity needs one person who can concentrate on the business and lead its management. It is important, both for me and for the company, that I concentrate on my greatest strengths -- the company's vision, the marketing and creative aspects of the business and its growth initiatives," Karan said in a statement announcing Idol's appointment.

Donna Karan has been struggling since it went public a year ago. In May it announced a restructuring that included a 4 percent cut in its workforce, a hiring freeze and steps to reduce its expenses by $4.8 million.
The company's stock slumped from a debut price of $24 all the way down to $8.75 earlier this year. It was at $11.75, up $1.3125 in late consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading.
The 38-year-old Idol comes to the troubled design house with strong credentials -- during his 13-year tenure, he helped develop the Ralph Lauren name into one of the leading designer brands.
Most recently, he oversaw Lauren's clothes, sheets, furniture and paint divisions, among others, that together accounted for $1.7 billion in annual revenues at Polo Ralph Lauren Corp.

Idol said his first priorities at Donna Karan are to increase shareholder value and profitability, especially through licensing deals, as well as by building more stand-alone stores in both the United States and overseas. There are currently more than 50 Donna Karan stores outside the United States and the company plans to open its first domestic store in Las Vegas around Thanksgiving.
"We plan to further exploit the opportunity of licensing alliances in the future. There is definitely an opportunity to grow that category," Idol told Reuters in an interview.
Analysts say the biggest challenge facing Idol may be negotiating with Karan herself, who is known for her hands-on management style.

"Idol comes with an impeccable pedigree. But the question is how much responsibility will he really have and how they work together on a day-to-day basis," said Alan Milstein, editor and publisher of the Fashion Network, an industry newsletter.
Donna Karan said she was confident in her choice and said Idol would have "full authority to lead and manage" the company.

"We worked hard to find the right person, one who I felt totally confident in and could really build the brand. I feel a lot more comfortable being able to concentrate my energies on what I do best -- design," she said in an interview.
The news of Idol's appointment could soothe angry shareholders, who have seen their investments lose nearly a third of their value since the company went public.
A group of shareholders slapped the company with a lawsuit in June, alleging the designer failed to disclose cost-control problems and hurt its income and ability to grow.
